appraisal.reasoning: Construction reads as typical mass-production Danish Modern casegoods: teak veneer over a composite/plywood carcass with solid teak edge banding and a carved integrated pull bar, rather than solid-teak studio furniture. No maker's mark, branding, or label is visible in any photo, and no back/drawer-interior shots are provided to confirm dovetail joinery, so this must be valued as an unattributed 'Danish Modern style' piece rather than a documented named-maker item, which caps both confidence and value. The design (floating cube nightstand with sculpted pull and open cubby) is extremely common and was produced by many Danish and Danish-influenced American manufacturers, so without a mark it competes with a crowded look-alike market. As a pair with visible finish wear (water rings, dulled top coat) but sound overall structure, realistic regional resale value is modest — local marketplace/eBay comps for unbranded teak-veneer Danish nightstand pairs in nice refinished condition typically land in the $450-650 range, not the $1,000+ seen on curated dealer sites. Restoration is straightforward and low-cost: strip/sand and re-oil or lacquer the tops to remove watermarks, spot-repair any veneer chips at edges, clean and wax hardware/pulls, and verify or add wall-mount brackets if intended for hanging use — roughly 6 hours of labor and under $150 in materials for the pair. Deal score is middling (50) reflecting a straightforward, low-risk flip with modest margin, contingent on the unknown asking price staying well under the ~$550 restored ceiling.
